o: (d) Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is c...
(c) Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is inc...
(b) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct...
(a) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct...
questions.e: By adding Part IX, the 73rd Amendment made the holding of regular elections and other provisions a constitutional obligation that can be enforced through courts, making it a landmark act.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Governor: 1️⃣ He submits his resignation letter to the Chief Justice of the state. 2️⃣ He should have completed 35 years of age. 3️⃣ His emoluments, allowances and privileges are determined by the President. 4️⃣ No criminal proceedings can be instituted against him.
questions.e: The Governor resigns to the President, not the Chief Justice. His emoluments are determined by the Parliament, not the President. He does enjoy immunity from criminal proceedings during his term.

questions.q: How many members are nominated to the State Legislative Council by the Governor?
questions.e: The Governor nominates 1/6th of the total members of the Legislative Council from among persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.

questions.q: Assertion: A minister at the state level continues in office till he enjoys the confidence of the Chief Minister. Reason: The Chief Minister can ask him to resign or advise the Governor to dismiss him in case of difference of opinion.
o: (b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
(a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
(c) A is true but R is false.
(d) A is false but R is true.
questions.e: Because the CM has the power to effectively end a minister's tenure via the Governor, the minister is said to hold office at the CM's "pleasure" in a political sense.

questions.q: Which of the following are true of the recommendations of Ashok Mehta Committee on Panchayati Raj? 1️⃣ Creation of Mandal Panchayat covering a population of 10,000 to 15,000. 2️⃣ The state legislature to have a committee on Panchayati Raj to look after the needs of weaker sections. 3️⃣ If Panchayati Raj institutions are superseded, elections must be held within one year. 4️⃣ Nyaya Panchayats should be presided over by the village development officer.
questions.e: The Ashok Mehta Committee's key unique recommendation was the Mandal Panchayat for a group of villages. Most of its other suggestions focused on strengthening Zila Parishads and involving political parties.

questions.q: Which of the following are true of the provisions of the 74th Amendment Act on municipalities? 1️⃣ Wards Committees, for wards with population of two lakhs. 2️⃣ The state Governor may authorise them to levy, collect and appropriate taxes. 3️⃣ A Municipal council for smaller Urban area. 4️⃣ The Twelfth Schedule contains 20 functional items for the municipalities.
questions.e: Wards Committees are for populations of 3 lakhs or more. The State Legislature (not Governor) authorizes taxes. The 12th Schedule contains 18 (not 20) items. Statement 3 correctly describes the Municipal Council.

questions.q: Assertion: The number of members of UPSC is determined by the President. Reason: The members of the UPSC are appointed by the President.
o: (b) Both A and R are true and R is not a correct explanation of A.
(c) A is true but R is false.
(a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
(d) A is false but R is true.
questions.e: Both are true as per the Constitution, but the power of appointment is distinct from the power to determine the size/strength of the commission.

questions.q: Assertion: The members of All-India Services work in the Central Government, state governments and union territories. Reason: They are selected and recruited on the basis of all-India competitive examinations conducted by the UPSC.
o: (d) A is false but R is true.
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
(a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
(c) A is true but R is false.
questions.e: The mode of recruitment (all-India exam) ensures a common standard, but their mobility between Union and States is a functional feature of the "dual control" system of All-India Services.

questions.q: Assertion: The principle of the rule of lapse leads to 'rush of expenditure' towards the end of a financial year. Reason: The unspent voted expenditure would lapse by the end of the financial year.
o: (d) A is false but R is true.
(c) A is true but R is false.
(a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
questions.e: Under the rule of lapse, any grant not spent by March 31st returns to the Consolidated Fund. To avoid losing the money, departments often spend heavily in the final weeks ("March Rush").

questions.q: Match List-I (Committees) with List-II (Created in): 1️⃣ A. Committee on Government Assurances - 4. 1953 2️⃣ B. Committee on Public Undertakings - 5. 1964 3️⃣ C. Committee on Subordinate Legislation - 2. 1953 4️⃣ D. Public Accounts Committee - 3. 1921
questions.e: PAC is the oldest (1921); Assurances and Subordinate Legislation were formed in 1953; and CPU was the latest to be established in 1964.

questions.q: Which of the following are true of Central Vigilance Commission? 1️⃣ It was set up on the recommendation of Santhanam Committee. 2️⃣ It does not exercise superintendence over the functioning of CBI. 3️⃣ It is set up by an executive resolution of the Government of India. 4️⃣ It consists of a chairman and three members.
questions.e: CVC does exercise superintendence over the CBI in anti-corruption matters. It consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two (not three) Vigilance Commissioners.

questions.q: Which of the following will be the consequences of declaration of national emergency by the President? 1️⃣ The Centre can issue directives to the state executives. 2️⃣ The President can extend the normal tenure of the Lok Sabha. 3️⃣ The President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of citizens. 4️⃣ The President can modify the distribution pattern of financial resources between Centre and states.
questions.e: Under Art 359, the President cannot suspend the right to move the court for enforcement of Articles 20 and 21. All other points are valid consequences of a National Emergency.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.e: The Portfolio system was recognized in 1861. Dyarchy at the Centre was 1935; Bicameralism at center was 1919; and G-G of India was 1833.

questions.q: Which of the following are true of the President's ordinance making power? 1️⃣ It is laid down in Article 123. 2️⃣ Its ambit is coextensive with the legislative power of Parliament. 3️⃣ He can promulgate an ordinance only when the Lok Sabha is not in session. 4️⃣ It is a discretionary power of the President.
questions.e: An ordinance can be issued when either house is not in session. It is not a discretionary power; the President acts only on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: Which of the following are the limitations on the sovereignty of Indian Parliament? 1️⃣ Fundamental Rights 2️⃣ Judicial Review 3️⃣ Federalism 4️⃣ Written Constitution
questions.e: Unlike the British Parliament, the Indian Parliament is limited by the supremacy of the written Constitution, the federal division of powers, the presence of justiciable Fundamental Rights, and the power of Courts to review laws.

questions.q: Assertion: Under the Government of India Act of 1935, the Residuary powers were vested in the Central Legislature. Reason: The Government of India Act of 1935 divided the subjects into three lists viz. the federal, provincial and concurrent.
o: (b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.

questions.e: Under the 1935 Act, residuary powers were given to the Governor-General, not the legislature. The division into three lists is a correct fact.

questions.q: Which of the following are the federal features of the Indian Constitution? 1️⃣ Rigid Constitution 2️⃣ Bicameral legislature 3️⃣ Office of the CAG 4️⃣ Collective responsibility 5️⃣ Office of the Governor
questions.e: Rigid Constitution and Bicameralism (representing states) are federal features. CAG, Governor, and Collective Responsibility are either unitary or parliamentary features.

questions.q: Assertion: The President of India determines the qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission. Reason: The Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are appointed by the President of India.
o: (b) Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
(c) A is true but R is false.
(a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
(d) A is false but R is true.
questions.e: Under Article 280, the Parliament (not the President) determines the qualifications of the members of the Finance Commission. They are, however, appointed by the President.

questions.q: The correct statements about Finance Commission are: 1️⃣ It is to act as the balancing wheel of Indian fiscal federalism 2️⃣ It consists of a chairman and three other members. 3️⃣ Qualifications of the members of the Commission are determined by the President. 4️⃣ It is constituted under the provisions of Article 280.
questions.e: The Commission consists of a Chairman and 4 (not 3) members. Qualifications are set by Parliament. It is indeed a balancing wheel in central-state financial relations.

questions.q: The Indian President's veto power is a combination of: 1️⃣ Pocket veto 2️⃣ Absolute veto 3️⃣ Suspensive veto 4️⃣ Qualified veto
questions.e: The Indian President possesses Absolute, Suspensive, and Pocket vetoes. Qualified veto (overridden by higher majority) is used in the US but not in India.

questions.q: The present relationship between the President and the council of ministers is governed by the provisions of:
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) amended Art 74 to allow the President to require the Council of Ministers to reconsider their advice, though the reconsidered advice is binding.

questions.q: The Zonal Councils have been established by:
o: (d) An order of the President of India
questions.e: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established by the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, not constitutional bodies.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ Parliament can increase a tax. 2️⃣ Parliament cannot reduce a tax. 3️⃣ Parliament can abolish a tax. 4️⃣ Parliament cannot increase a tax. 5️⃣ Parliament can reduce a tax.
questions.e: Under Article 117, Parliament can reduce or abolish a tax, but it cannot increase a tax beyond what is proposed in the budget by the executive.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are correct with regard to the expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India? 1️⃣ It is subject to the vote of Parliament. 2️⃣ It is subject to the discussion in Parliament. 3️⃣ It is subject to the vote of Lok Sabha only. 4️⃣ It is not subject to the vote of Parliament.
questions.e: The Constitution specifically exempts certain expenditures from the voting process to ensure independence, though they remain open to parliamentary discussion.

questions.q: The correct statements regarding the difference between the pardoning powers of President and Governor are: 1️⃣ The Governor can pardon sentences inflicted by court martial while the President cannot. 2️⃣ The President can pardon death sentence while Governor cannot. 3️⃣ The Governor can pardon death sentence while the President cannot. 4️⃣ The President can pardon sentences inflicted by court martial while the Governor cannot.
questions.e: Only the President has the power to pardon death sentences and sentences passed by a Court Martial. The Governor's power doesn't extend to these two areas.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the powers of a Governor to reserve a bill for the consideration of the President? 1️⃣ It is laid down in Article 200. 2️⃣ It is not a discretionary power of the Governor. 3️⃣ It is compulsory, if the bill endangers the position of High Court.
questions.e: Under Article 200, the Governor has the discretion to reserve any bill. However, it is mandatory to reserve a bill that would derogate from the powers of the High Court.

questions.q: The incorrect statements about Central Vigilance Commission are: 1️⃣ It was set up on the recommendations of First Administrative Reforms Commission of India. 2️⃣ It is headed by the Central Vigilance Commissioner appointed by the Prime Minister. 3️⃣ Its functions, in certain cases, overlap with the functions of the UPSC. 4️⃣ It is certainly a substitute for an Ombudsman. 5️⃣ It receives complaints directly from aggrieved persons.
questions.e: CVC was recommended by Santhanam Committee (not ARC). The Commissioner is appointed by the President (not PM). It is an anti-corruption body, not a general ombudsman.

questions.q: Which of the following civil services find mention in the Constitution? 1️⃣ Indian Administrative Service 2️⃣ Indian Forest Service 3️⃣ Indian Police Service 4️⃣ All-India Judicial Service 5️⃣ Indian Foreign Service
questions.e: Article 312 mentions IAS and IPS. It also mentions the creation of an All-India Judicial Service. IFoS was created in 1966 under Art 312 but isn't specifically named in the text of the Constitution.

questions.q: In which of the following circumstances, the President can remove a member of the UPSC without referring the matter to the Supreme Court? 1️⃣ If he engages, during his term of office, in any paid employment outside the duties of his office. 2️⃣ If he is adjudged an insolvent. 3️⃣ If he is unfit to continue in office by reason of infirmity of mind or body. 4️⃣ If he becomes, in any way, concerned or interested in any contract or agreement made by or on behalf of the Government of India or the government of a state.
questions.e: For cases of "misbehaviour" (Point 4), the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court. For insolvency, outside employment, or infirmity, the President can act directly under Article 317.

questions.q: Which of the following are not the concerns of the UPSC? 1️⃣ Classification of services 2️⃣ Promotion 3️⃣ Training 4️⃣ Disciplinary matters 5️⃣ Talent hunting
questions.e: UPSC is primarily a recruiting agency (talent hunting) and is consulted on promotion and disciplinary matters. Classification of services and training are handled by the Department of Personnel and Training.

questions.q: Match List-I (Acts) with List-II (Provisions): 1️⃣ A. Indian Councils Act of 1861 - 3. Introduced representative institutions 2️⃣ B. Government of India Act of 1919 - 1. Introduced Dyarchy 3️⃣ C. Indian Councils Act of 1892 - 5. Introduced principle of election 4️⃣ D. Pitt's India Act of 1784 - 2. Placed Indian affairs under direct British control
questions.e: The 1861 Act was a landmark in legislative history; 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy; 1892 was the first step toward elections; 1784 established the dual system of control.

questions.q: Statement-I: NITI Aayog is neither a statutory body nor a constitutional body. Statement-II: It is established by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet.
o: (c) Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is inc...
(b) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct...

questions.q: Which of the following writs is not specifically provided in the Constitution of India?
questions.e: The Constitution specifically mentions five writs under Articles 32 and 226: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-warranto. Injunction is a general legal remedy but not one of the five specific constitutional writs.
